title: Choose offsite backup storage provider
description: Decide where the offsite copy of the restic repositories lives before implementing the copy itself. Compare Backblaze B2, S3-compatible object storage and a second physical site/NAS on cost, egress, restic/rclone support, credential handling via sops, encryption, and how the restore drill reaches it. Record the decision and its rationale in this bead; the implementation is nix-workloads-o1m.
acceptance_criteria: A provider/site is chosen and recorded with rationale, rough monthly cost, egress/restore implications, and the sops/age credential path. nix-workloads-o1m is then unblocked.

title: Copy restic backups offsite
description: Known risk: losing both Pi hosts loses everything. Attic/restic repos only exist on rpi5-4gb. Add an offsite copy (B2/S3/second site) and include it in the restore drill.

title: Pilot: reimplement one Node-RED flow as HA YAML in dev
description: Pick one representative existing Node-RED flow (for example a light or heating schedule with a condition) and reimplement it as an HA YAML/Nix automation in dev. Compare agent authoring, diff and review, config validation, deploy/rollback, and debugging against the Node-RED flow. Record what was easy, what was hard, and whether HA YAML covers the common cases. Do not change homelab flows yet.
acceptance_criteria: One real flow runs in dev as HA YAML; config check passes; the change is diffable and reviewable; notes on authoring, testing, debugging and gaps versus Node-RED; a recommendation to nix-workloads-a7q.

title: Apply minimal config and retire experiment tuning
description: Deploy the reduced workload config in dev, verify, then homelab; rebuild hosts; run doctor/verify/snapshots; watch OOM, PSI and NVMe swap for 24-48h. Remove dead experiment scaffolding (density KSM panels and stale baseline text) and close E1-E5.
acceptance_criteria: Dev and homelab verification pass; 48h clean (no OOM, no PSI rise, no disk-swap growth); config is smaller than before; experiment beads closed; dashboards/docs reflect the steady state.

title: Return host memory/zram settings to simple defaults
description: In nix-homelab-hosts, prefer upstream/NixOS defaults over experiment-era zram/swappiness/page-cluster/PSI tweaks for the mostly-idle 8GB/4GB pair. Remove KSM and any density experiment knobs; keep PSI only if it is still useful. Document why any remaining non-default exists and how to roll back.
acceptance_criteria: Host memory/zram config is at least as simple as stock; any remaining non-default is justified; hosts rebuilt; task doctor/verify pass; no disk-swap or NVMe regression.

title: Delete unnecessary workload overrides; keep only measured exceptions
description: Start from the shared container profile and remove per-guest memory/swap/OOM overrides that the baseline does not justify. Keep an override only for a measured spike or to protect HA/MQTT/zigbee2mqtt. Prefer deleting over adjusting. Reconcile E1/E2/E3/E5; update inventory comments/README if the policy changes. Dev deploy+verify first, then homelab.
acceptance_criteria: Each remaining override has a one-line reason; the diff is mostly deletions; dev verify passes; rollout plan recorded; experiment beads reconciled.

title: Measure only enough to justify deletions (7/30 days)
description: Find what actually needs an override, not a tuning matrix. Over 7 and 30 days, pull per-guest p95/p99 memory current/anon/file, OOM and swap-cap events, PSI and refaults, plus host MemAvailable, zram and NVMe writes. Flag only outliers and the critical services that need protection; everything else is a candidate for deleting its override.
acceptance_criteria: A short list of guests with a measured need plus host headroom, with queries/window; an explicit list of overrides that can be removed; no fine-grained per-guest tuning proposals.

title: Minimize resource tuning for a mostly idle homelab
description: The fleet is mostly idle and the current limits, swap caps, OOM priorities and zram settings are leftovers from the density experiments (E1-E7). Bias toward tuning as little as possible: delete experiment-era overrides, return to upstream/NixOS defaults where safe, and keep only overrides that a measurement or a concrete protection need justifies. The target is a smaller, simpler config - not a finely tuned one. If a workload is fine on the shared profile and the host has headroom, remove its override. Dev-first, then homelab.
acceptance_criteria: Fewer overrides than today; every remaining limit/swap/OOM/host knob has a recorded reason (measured need or critical-service protection); defaults are documented; dev deploy+verify and homelab doctor/verify pass; no OOM, PSI rise or disk-swap growth; E1-E5 reconciled.

title: Choose an agent-maintainable automation model
description: Agents now do most of the automation work; Node-RED was chosen for a human editing flows in a UI. Decide the authoring/runtime model for the next phase, keeping the runtime deterministic for lights and heating while agents author, review, test and deploy. Options: HA YAML/Nix automations (best text, diff and test ergonomics; native), AppDaemon/Python (complex logic), Node-RED flows-as-code (keeps the visual engine but JSON is noisy for agents), n8n/Windmill (UI plus code but heavier), and agent-at-runtime (ad-hoc only). Recommendation: pilot HA YAML for the common cases, keep Node-RED only for flows that need it, then decide migrate versus split. The pilot is nix-workloads-i5v.
acceptance_criteria: A model is chosen and recorded after the pilot: where each class of automation lives (HA YAML, Node-RED, code), how agents author, review, test and deploy it, how credentials and rollback work, and whether Node-RED is retained, shrunk or retired. The runtime for lights and heating remains deterministic.

title: Migrate Home Assistant automations to YAML packages in the repo
description: HA is UI-configured (.storage), so agents can read but not diff or review automations. Move automations/scripts to services.home-assistant.config packages, add config check to verify, and keep the .storage migration path in README.

title: Run replicated S3 storage (Garage) on both hosts
description: Run an S3-compatible object store as incus workloads on both rpi5-8gb and rpi5-4gb, replicated so the data survives either host failing. Primary use: move OpenTofu state off the Mac's local terraform.tfstate (currently gitignored) and give other S3-compatible data a home. Evaluate Garage (preferred for two-node replication), SeaweedFS and MinIO; decide engine, topology (Garage layout vs bucket replication), capacity/CPU/memory on the Pis, TLS via step-ca, and sops credentials. Solve the bootstrap chicken-and-egg: OpenTofu cannot create the store that holds its own state without a documented local/bootstrap state path and migration. Replication is not offsite - nix-workloads-o1m remains separate. Test in dev first.
acceptance_criteria: Engine and replication topology chosen; both hosts serve the store in dev; OpenTofu backend configured with state migrated and a documented bootstrap/restore path when one host is down; credentials via sops; capacity and memory limits recorded; restore drill covers it; offsite copy explicitly out of scope.

title: E8: btrfs dedup of container rootfs
description: duperemove dry-run then apply over container subvolumes, excluding DB volumes. Disk-only density (not anon memory). Details: EXPERIMENTS.md E8.
close_reason: Complete 2026-10-18: duperemove reduced btrfs used 23.81 GiB to 19.15 GiB (~4.66 GiB); not reversible.

title: Close out E3 swap-cap experiment (monitoring 256 to 512 MiB)
description: Raise monitoring limits.memory.swap from 256MiB to 512MiB to prove zram absorbs the extra swap without touching the NVMe. Watch swap_events_max/fail, zram ratio, mem_used, PSI; guardrail NVMe write slope. Details: EXPERIMENTS.md E3.
notes: Applied 2026-10-18 16:07 UTC; swap events/high/max/fail were still 0, swap use ~167 MiB and zram RAM ~196 MiB at the time. Needs a final keep/revert.

title: Close out E1/E2 cache rebalance
description: E1 gives cache back to the refaulting guests; E2 trims cold cache from the quiet guests. Both change the inventory.nix memory table and are treated as one rebalance. Hypothesis, exact changes, watch/guardrail and rollback: EXPERIMENTS.md E1/E2.
notes: Observation window started 2026-10-18 ~15:35 UTC. Historical measurements are in EXPERIMENTS.md. Needs a final 24h+ comparison and an explicit keep/revert; E4 waits on this.

title: Make host maintenance and reboots safe for the home
description: Both rpi5-8gb and rpi5-4gb are standalone incus servers. Today a host reboot or upgrade can take internet/DNS, identity, MQTT/Zigbee and the lights/heating with it, even though most workloads could run on the other host. Define what must stay up and where it runs, then implement and rehearse a single-host maintenance path: move or duplicate critical services off the host being serviced, ensure guests auto-start, sequence reboots, and keep monitoring/alerting meaningful during the window. Accept an outage only where hardware pins a workload - notably the Zigbee USB dongle, which stays with its physical host. This is not full HA failover; it is safe, predictable maintenance.
acceptance_criteria: A documented, tested runbook for servicing either host, including the host with the Zigbee dongle: internet/DNS, MQTT/Zigbee (lights/heating) and identity stay available, or the unavoidable exception is explicitly listed. Guests auto-start after reboot; monitoring/alerts stay meaningful; verification and rollback steps are included; at least one maintenance window is rehearsed in dev and one in homelab.

title: Force host-level OOM priority ordering (E5)
description: Only the dev cgroup OOM path was validated; host-level priority ordering under real pressure is untested. See EXPERIMENTS.md E5.

title: Re-run zram tuning (E4) after E1/E2 settle
description: zram/swappiness change was reverted. Re-run once the E1/E2 cache rebalance observation window closes. See EXPERIMENTS.md E4.

title: Design shared Nix store (E9)
description: Shared Nix store across guests: design and reliability plan. See EXPERIMENTS.md E9.

title: Measure KSM before committing (E7)
description: Measure KSM savings and CPU cost on the Pi pair before enabling it fleet-wide. See EXPERIMENTS.md E7.
close_reason: Rejected 2026-10-18: ~40 MiB gross/~35 MiB net saving while ksmd burned ~6.7% of a core; reverted and the host/guest KSM code removed. Do not re-run without a new density hypothesis.

title: Replace or tune per-guest Alloy (E6)
description: grafana-alloy is the largest shared closure item (~360 MiB/guest). Decide: tune it or swap for node-exporter + a log shipper. See EXPERIMENTS.md E6.

title: Drop the Home Assistant nixpkgs band-aid when 26.11 ships HA 2026.9+
description: The home-assistant guest overlays HA from a pinned unstable revision (nixpkgs-ha input) to avoid downgrading .storage. Remove the input + overlay once NixOS 26.11 ships HA 2026.9+. See README 'Version pin (band-aid)'.
